rounds.text: Om Infra Ltd presents a compelling value opportunity anchored by a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to an intrinsic value of ₹ 140 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 43.6% against the current market price of ₹ 78.8 [E46, E47]. This mispricing is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio trading right at parity (0.99x) and sitting below the sector benchmark of 1.27x [E2, E7], despite the stock resting at a depressed 11% of its 52-week range [E5]. Fundamental momentum supports the bull thesis through a strong 5-year compounded sales growth of 16% and an impressive profit growth of 18.5% CAGR over the same period [E15, E61], outperforming the sector median sales growth of 7.1% [E79]. A reverse DCF reveals that the market price only prices in a modest 10.1% earnings growth, leaving plenty of room to beat the 18.0% base case assumption [E48]. Conceded: the company faces near-term headwinds with a 3-year compounded sales growth of -14% and a trailing twelve-month contraction of -20% [E16, E17], alongside an ROA of 2.25% that lags the sector benchmark of 4.2% [E8].

Om Infra Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are not supported by underlying fundamental trends. The company trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 23.07x, which represents a substantial premium over the sector benchmark of 14.65x [E6]. This elevated multiple rests on shaky ground given the severe deterioration in top-line growth: compounded sales growth has collapsed to -14% over 3 years and plunges further to -20% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17]. Furthermore, asset efficiency severely lags behind peers, with a return on assets of just 2.25% compared to the sector benchmark of 4.2% [E8]. Compounded over a longer ten-year horizon, sales growth crawls at a modest 8% [E14]. Compended by the stock sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 11% of its yearly high [E5], market sentiment reflects deep underlying weakness rather than confidence. Conceded: the company has delivered good profit growth of 18.5% CAGR over the last 5 years [E61] and trades near book value at 0.99x [E2].

Conceded: P/E is 23.07x against the sector benchmark of 14.65x [E6], and ROA is 2.25% versus 4.2% [E8]. However, the bear's focus on trailing growth ignores the multi-year trajectory, where 5-year compounded sales growth accelerates to 16% [E15] alongside a robust 18.5% CAGR in profit over the same period [E61]. The market price sits at just 0.99x book value [E2], aligning closely with the sector benchmark of 1.27x [E7] and offering substantial protection compared to the broader valuation narrative. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 140 leaves a large margin of safety of 43.6% against the current price of Rs 78.8 [E46, E47]. The reverse DCF shows that the price only demands a modest 10.1% earnings growth, which is easily cleared by the company's baseline performance [E48]. Finally, the stock sitting at 11% of its 52-week range [E5] reflects excessive pessimism, especially as recent momentum shows sales up 19% YoY [E69] and profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E72].

Conceded: 5-year compounded sales growth is 16% [E15] and profit CAGR over the same period is 18.5% [E61]. However, the bull's reliance on multi-year trajectory glosses over a severe and sharp contraction in the short term, specifically 3-year compounded sales growth of -14% [E16] and trailing twelve months sales growth of -20% [E17]. While the price sits at 0.99x book value [E2] and near the bottom of its 52-week range at 11% [E5], this depression in price is fully justified by weak asset efficiency, evidenced by an ROA of 2.25% that lags far behind the sector benchmark of 4.2% [E8]. Furthermore, the premium P/E of 23.07x heavily penalizes shareholders relative to the sector benchmark of 14.65x [E6], conflicting directly with the lower asset returns. Finally, the bull's reliance on a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 140 [E46] ignores the signal engine warning that price has historically grown faster than profit over a 5-year span, signalling that the stock has run ahead of its fundamentals [E57].
